title: El interlocal a Masaya
desc: Leaving Managua for the first time
setting: You are at the interlocal terminal and everybody seems to know something you do not.

steps.speaker: Ayudante
steps.en: Masaya, Masaya! Are you going to Masaya?

options.en: Yes, I am. How much is the fare?
options.feedback: You are on the right bus and you asked the price. Both of those are yours to ask.
Enough to get you on board, but you have not asked the price and it is your right to.

options.en: Is this the bus to León?
options.feedback: He has shouted Masaya four times. Listen before you ask.

steps.speaker: Ayudante
steps.en: Thirty-five. Get in at the front.

options.en: Here you go. Will you let me know when we arrive?
options.feedback: Paid, and asked the man who knows. That is exactly what an ayudante is there for.
You have paid and boarded. Asking him to tell you is what a first-timer should do.
You have not handed him anything yet.

steps.speaker: Ayudante
steps.es: Tranquilo, yo le aviso. ¿Primera vez que va?
steps.en: Relax, I will tell you. First time going?

options.es: Sí, primera vez. Voy al mercado de artesanía.
options.en: Yes, first time. I am going to the craft market.
options.feedback: Saying it is your first time costs nothing and buys you somebody watching out for your stop.
True, and it closes a conversation he opened to help you.

options.en: No, I go all the time.
options.feedback: A small lie that costs you the help he was about to give.

steps.speaker: Ayudante
steps.es: Ah, entonces se baja conmigo. Yo también voy allá.
steps.en: Ah, then you get off with me. I am going there too.

options.en: That is good. Thank you very much.
options.feedback: Warm and easy, and vos is right with somebody your own age.
It accepts, but flatly, and he just did you a favour.

options.en: No need, I will watch out.
options.feedback: You have just turned down a guide on your first trip out of the city.
